half_life_summaries: DualAG: 1.7 h (mouse plasma (circulating bioactive peptide, lean C57Bl/6 mice)) ; oxyntomodulin (OXM), native: ~8–12 min (not reported (stated only as in vivo T1/2 for native OXM))
bioanalytical_method: In vitro cell-based cAMP bioassay of GLP1R agonist potency (CHO cells stably transfected with human GLP1R), quantified against a standard curve of peptide spiked into mouse plasma
notes: PK values are reported only for DualAG, and only in a single RESULTS sentence: Tmax 5 h and T1/2 1.7 h after 3 mg/kg s.c. in lean C57Bl/6 mice. No error terms, no group size, no AUC and no numeric Cmax are given for the PK study; 'peak plasma peptide concentrations (Cmax) were achieved ∼5 h after subcutaneous injection' reports a time, not a concentration, so cmax is recorded as not reported. GLPAG PK is described only qualitatively as comparable to DualAG. The paper reports a single half-life without naming a phase, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and both half_life_absorption and half_life_elimination are left 'not reported' per protocol; do not read 1.7 h as a fitted elimination-phase value. DISCREPANCY with the PEPLIFE2 header rows: the header lists Oxm at '~8-12 hours', but the body twice states minutes ('T1/2 ∼12 min' in INTRO, '∼8–12 min for native OXM' in RESULTS); the body value in minutes is recorded here. The header also lists the assay as RP-HPLC and ESI-MS; in the body RP-HPLC and electrospray MS were used for peptide synthesis, purification and characterisation, while plasma peptide concentrations were measured by a cell-based cAMP bioassay. Sequences were not extracted because the PEPLIFE2 header is database metadata and the body does not print the amino-acid sequences. Roles: dextrose is a metabolic challenge agent rather than a test article; the protocol role enum does not cover this, so 'other' is used. Anaesthetics (isofluorane) are procedural and are not listed as agents.

half_life_summaries: cyclic chlorotoxin:Cy5.5 (cyclized CTX:Cy5.5): 11 h (mouse serum/plasma after a single intravenous injection) ; native (linear) chlorotoxin:Cy5.5 (CTX:Cy5.5): approximately 14 h (mouse serum (value stated as known in advance of the current studies, i.e. from prior work))

notes: Only cyclic CTX:Cy5.5 was pharmacokinetically profiled in this study (11 h, no error term). The ~14 h half-life for linear CTX:Cy5.5 is stated in the body as prior knowledge ('We knew, in advance of the current studies') rather than as data generated here, and no dose, group size or error term is given for it. No Cmax, tmax, AUC or clearance is reported for any agent. Doses are given as volume x molarity (50 uL of 40 uM) with no mg/kg equivalent. No amino-acid sequences appear in the body text; Fig. 1B is stated to contain them but the figure image is not available in this text file. The half-life measures the Cy5.5 fluorescent signal, not intact peptide.

half_life_summaries: RMP16 (recombinant slow-release TNF alpha-derived peptide): 13.100 ± 1.49 h (Table 2); stated as 13.1 h in the Results text (BALB/c mouse plasma) ; P16 (TNF alpha segment, residues 75-94): 0.096 ± 0.008 h (Table 2); stated as 5.76 min in the Results text (BALB/c mouse plasma) ; TNF alpha (recombinant human): 0.56 ± 0.13 h (Table 2); stated as 33.6 min in the Results text (BALB/c mouse plasma)
bioanalytical_method: LC/MS/MS with electrospray ionization; standard curves prepared in citrated mouse plasma (2000 to 4 nM) with TCEP added to enhance peptide recovery; acetonitrile protein precipitation

The Table 2 'Units' column gives 'h' for t1/2 and the Methods explicitly name the fitted parameter 'elimination half-life (t1/2)' from a two-compartment elimination model in WinNonlin, so these are half-lives in hours, not rate constants, and half_life_phase is 'elimination'. Dosing was intravenous, so no absorption phase exists or is reported. Results text and Table 2 agree (0.096 h = 5.76 min; 0.56 h = 33.6 min). A separate in vitro Factor Xa digestion half-life for RMP16 is also reported - 'the factor Xa enzyme digestion half-life of RMP16 was significantly prolonged to 15.83 h from 9.72 h' in the presence of HSA - but this is a cell-free enzymatic stability value, not a plasma half-life, and is deliberately not placed in any agent half_life field. Cmax and tmax are not reported for any agent. The PK cohort strain is given only as 'BALB/c mice'; the tumour study used BALB/c-nu/nu nude mice. TNF alpha half-life figures quoted in the INTRO and DISCUSSION (15-30 min, ~30 min) are literature statements, not this study's measurements, so the Table 2 value is used. Role 'other' is not used here; H398 is recorded as a comparator because it is a pharmacological blocking agent tested alongside RMP16.

half_life_summaries: IONP-HA-GEM-CTX-Cy5.5 (iron oxide nanoparticle bearing gemcitabine and chlorotoxin via hyaluronic acid, labelled with Cy5.5): ~2.8 h (blood half-life) (mouse blood (Cy5.5 fluorescence of blood samples)) ; Gemcitabine (GEM), free drug: not reported in this study's own experiments; the Introduction cites a literature value of ~0.28 h (human and mouse blood (cited literature value, not measured here))

notes: This is a short communication: the Methods are in Supplementary Information and are not part of the provided body, so mouse strain, sex, age, exact sampling times, number of animals in the biodistribution and BBB arms, and formal PK modelling details are not reported in the body. half_life_summaries: Api88: 17.3 min (i.p. 5 mg/kg) and 11.1 min (i.p. 20 mg/kg) (mouse plasma (female NMRI, intraperitoneal)) ; Api137: 33.8 min (i.p. 5 mg/kg) and 16.9 min (i.p. 20 mg/kg) (mouse plasma (female NMRI, intraperitoneal)) ; Onc72: not reported for this study in vivo; body cites a previously reported mouse serum half-life of ~3 h and reports >89% intact after 1 h in peritoneal lavage (mouse peritoneal lavage (ex vivo)) ; Onc112: not reported for this study in vivo; body cites a previously reported in vitro mouse serum half-life exceeding 8 h and reports >89% intact after 1 h in peritoneal lavage (mouse peritoneal lavage (ex vivo))
bioanalytical_method: RP-HPLC (Alliance 2695) coupled online to ESI-QqLIT-MS (4000 QTRAP with TurboV ion-spray source) in positive multiple reaction monitoring mode, quantified against isotope-labelled peptide standards (LOQ 19–59 ng/mL); metabolite identification by nanoACQUITY UPLC coupled to ESI-LTQ Orbitrap XL MS; peritoneal lavage stability by RP-HPLC with UV absorbance at 214 nm
concentration_time_locator: Fig. 2A (i.v. plasma); Fig. 3A,B (i.p. plasma); Fig. 4 (kidney and liver homogenates); Fig. 5 (urine); Fig. 7 (peritoneal lavage % remaining)
notes: All PK parameters were taken from Table 1 and the Results body. Table 1 reports single mean values without error terms, calculated with PKSolver 'using the concentrations for the terminal elimination phase determined by the software'. Half-lives are route- and dose-dependent: i.p. 5 mg/kg gives 17.3 min (Api88) and 33.8 min (Api137); i.p. 20 mg/kg gives 11.1 min and 16.9 min. No half-life was calculated for the intravenous route; after i.v. 5 mg/kg, plasma levels fell to around the LOQ by 10 min (Api88 1 μg/mL and Api137 0.4 μg/mL at 5 min). No Tmax is tabulated; maxima coincided with the earliest sampling times. Group-size discrepancy: Methods state n = 4 per time point per peptide for the i.v. CD-1 study while the Fig. 2 caption states n = 5; Fig. 4 states n = 5 organs while the i.p. Methods state n = 7. The frequently quoted in vitro mouse serum half-lives (~5 min for Api88, ~6 h for Api137, ~3 h for Onc72, >8 h for Onc112) appear in the Introduction and Discussion but are explicitly attributed to earlier publications (Berthold et al.; Czihal et al.; Knappe et al.) and were not measured in this study, so no in vitro study type is recorded. Likewise the MIC values (~4 μg/mL against E. coli ATCC 25922) and ribosome Kd values are cited from prior work. Onc72 and Onc112 were tested here only ex vivo in peritoneal lavage; their in vivo efficacy data are cited from Schmidt et al.

half_life_summaries: cRGD-ZW800-1: 71.1 ± 9.4 min (mean terminal half-life) (mouse serum (peripheral blood, tumour-free mice))
bioanalytical_method: NIR fluorescence measurement of whole blood in 60 microL capillary tubes using the FLARE imaging system at multiple exposure times, back-calculated against a mouse-serum calibration curve; PK analysis in NONMEM
notes: Cmax/tmax ARE reported here: maximal serum concentration 1.17 microM measured at 1 minute post injection (the first post-dose sampling point of a -5/1/6/10/20/30/40/50/60/90/120/240 min schedule), so tmax is the earliest sample rather than a fitted peak. No absorption half-life exists for this study because dosing was intravenous. CONFLICTING HALF-LIVES IN THE BODY: the Results give a mean terminal half-life of 71.1 ± 9.4 min, while the Discussion refers to a 'mean blood half-life of 25 min' with no phase label. Both are in the body; the named terminal value was taken as the headline. The 25.3 ± 6.4 min and 14.6 ± 1.7 min (distribution) values in the PEPLIFE2 header are database metadata; the distribution half-life is referenced in the body only as 'see Supplementary Table 2', so it is recorded as not reported. AUC is mentioned in the Figure 6 caption but no numeric value appears in the body. Sequence: the body calls cRGD-ZW800-1 a 'cyclic pentapeptide' and never prints the amino acid sequence; the 'RGDyK' string comes only from the PEPLIFE2 metadata block and was not used. Substances mentioned but excluded from agents, with reasons: ZW800-1 dye alone (evaluated at 24.5 mg/kg but explicitly 'unpublished data'); a rat toxicology study of cRGD-ZW800-1 at 5.0 mg/kg i.v., also explicitly 'unpublished data' - rat is therefore not listed in in_vivo_species; isoflurane (anaesthetic), propidium iodide, ToPro3 and anti-integrin/isotype antibodies (assay reagents). Ex vivo classification is based on the mouse-serum calibration curve (compound added to serum outside the body) and on ex vivo imaging of excised organs and tumours.

half_life_summaries: KP-54 (human kisspeptin-54): around 32 min (mouse plasma) ; KP-10 (human kisspeptin-10 / Metastin 45-54 amide): about 4 min (mouse plasma)
bioanalytical_method: In-house competitive radioimmunoassay (RIA) using sheep polyclonal antibody GQ2 raised against human KP-54
notes: Both Cmax and tmax are reported in the body for both peptides: KP-10 248 ± 9 pmol/l at 2 min; KP-54 12292 ± 2655 pmol/l at 5 min. Half-lives are given as approximate values with no error terms and no named phase, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and both phase-specific fields are left 'not reported' - the paper does not fit or report a two-phase model. The authors caveat the KP-54 value: the RIA recognises all forms of kisspeptin, so the measured 32 min may partly reflect immunoreactive breakdown products; and they speculate that the apparent short half-life of KP-10 may reflect sequestration by serum proteins. Human KP-54 and KP-10 were used because the RIA does not detect mouse kisspeptins. The 3.8 min and 28 min human values quoted in the Discussion are literature comparisons, not measurements from this study, and are not recorded as agent values. Sequences are not printed in the body, so they are 'not reported' despite the PEPLIFE2 header listing them. BSA-FITC is a blood-brain-barrier tracer and dextrose-like challenge agents are not covered by the protocol role enum, so 'other' is used. Procedural agents (pentobarbital anaesthesia/euthanasia, paraformaldehyde perfusion) are not listed as tested substances.

half_life_summaries: Api88: around 1 hour in fresh mouse blood (this study); less than 5 min in mouse serum (cited prior work) (fresh CD-1 mouse blood (ex vivo); mouse serum for the cited <5 min value) ; Api134: 4 h in mouse serum (cited prior work); no new half-life value determined here (mouse serum) ; Api137: 6 h in mouse serum (cited prior work); no new half-life value determined here (mouse serum) ; Onc18: 20 min in serum per Results; 25 min in mouse serum per Discussion (both cited prior work); no new half-life value determined here (mouse serum) ; Onc72: 3 h in mouse serum (cited prior work); no new half-life value determined here (mouse serum) ; Onc112: more than 8 h in mouse serum (cited prior work); no new half-life value determined here (mouse serum)
bioanalytical_method: RP-HPLC with UV detection at 214 nm (Jupiter C18) for quantification of intact peptide relative to time zero; LC coupled on-line to electrospray-ionization ion-trap MS (Agilent 1100 / Bruker Esquire HCT) for metabolite identification and quantification; MALDI-TOF/TOF-MS for monoisotopic mass confirmation of synthesized peptides
notes: This study contains NO in vivo dosing. Mice were euthanized and terminally bled by cardiac puncture into a syringe that already contained the peptide solution, so all peptide exposure is ex vivo. in_vivo_species is therefore an empty array. The PeplLife2 metadata labels these rows 'In Vitro'; per the protocol's definition, blood/serum/plasma degradation assays are ex vivo (the human alpha-thrombin digestion in S3 Fig is the only genuinely in vitro exposure). None of the eight peptides had a half-life measured in this study; the qualitative PeplLife2 descriptors (Highly/Medium/Low Stable) correspond to Table 3 'Stability of eight peptides in fresh blood, serum, and plasma' (High: Api134/Api137/Onc112; Medium: Onc18/Onc72; Low: Api88/AAYR-Onc112/LVPR-Onc112). The numeric half-lives quoted in the body (Api88 <5 min, Api134 4 h, Api137 6 h, Onc18 20 min in Results but 25 min in Discussion, Onc72 3 h, Onc112 >8 h, all in mouse serum) are explicitly attributed to earlier publications, not measured here; note the internal 20 vs 25 min discrepancy for Onc18. The statement that 'Onc112 exhibited an improved pharmacokinetic profile and around fivefold higher plasma levels than Onc72 after intravenous application in mice' is likewise cited prior work. Peptide concentration in every matrix was ~31.5 umol/L; blood volume drawn into the peptide syringe was 200-300 uL. Sampling: 1 and 60 min in blood (1, 10 and 30 min for Api88); 0 and 60 min in serum/plasma (0, 10 and 30 min for Api88). Replication: 'at least in triplicates' for stability tests, and 'Six to nine samples were analyzed for each matrix' for the fibrinopeptide A analysis. Api137 was used as an internal 100%-stability reference to bound a ~10% matrix-effect error in the blood samples.

half_life_summaries: [18F]FPCA-F9 solution (18F-labelled F9 monomer): not reported (no blood or plasma half-life is given for the monomer) (None) ; [18F]FPCA-F9 hydrogel (18F-labelled F9 co-assembled with unfunctionalised F9): not reported for the radiolabelled hydrogel (None) ; FITC-F9 hydrogel (fluorescein isothiocyanate N-terminal labelled F9 in unfunctionalised F9 hydrogel): between 1 and 4 days (biological half-life of the F9 hydrogel) (subcutaneous hydrogel depot at the injection site (FITC fluorescence signal intensity), not plasma) ; Unfunctionalised F9 peptide (hydrogel matrix): not measured directly; the F9 hydrogel biological half-life was inferred from FITC-F9 signal as between 1 and 4 days (subcutaneous hydrogel depot at the injection site)

bioanalytical_method: not reported
notes: The supplied full-text file contains no METHODS or Experimental Section, so the bioanalytical assay, the exact PK dose and the PK sampling schedule are not recoverable from the body. The PEPLIFE2 header lists the assay as LC-MS/SIM; that is database metadata and was not used, so bioanalytical_method is recorded as not reported. Over 80 cyclic d,l-alpha-peptides were screened (81 sequences per the Results text, with 73 eight-residue and 8 six-residue peptides); only the sequences printed in the body text or in Table 1 are captured as agent objects, and the remainder are listed only in Table S1, which is not part of the supplied body. Peptides 1, 15, 18, 23-26, 33, 34, 36-39, 41-50 and 52-54 are discussed by number in the Results without their sequences being printed. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), given intraperitoneally to induce the acute inflammation model, is a model-induction agent and is noted here rather than listed as an agent object.

notes: The only PK parameter in the body is the blood elimination half-life of SNIO–CBP (5.7 ± 1.9 min, n = 3 normal male mice, 2 nmol/g CBP i.v.), derived from a monoexponential fit of MRI blood-pool CNR rather than from measured plasma concentrations; no Cmax, Tmax, AUC, clearance or volume of distribution is reported, and no plasma assay of the agent was performed. The CBP amino-acid sequence is never printed in the body (only the PeplifeDB metadata header lists one, which per protocol cannot be used). CM-101 has no numeric PK in the body, only a qualitative statement of similarity. CCl4 and olive oil are listed as agents because they were administered, but they are disease-induction/vehicle-control treatments rather than test articles. The FBS incubation is recorded as ex vivo per protocol, though it assessed nonspecific protein binding rather than stability. Total of 35 mice studied.

half_life_summaries: HM-10/10: 5.68 min (CD-1 mouse plasma (K2EDTA, previously frozen)) ; Lovastatin: 14.4 min (CD-1 mouse plasma) ; Propantheline: 70.4 min (CD-1 mouse plasma) ; Verapamil: 6.53 min (CD-1 mouse liver microsomes); 20.2 min (CD-1 mouse hepatocytes) (CD-1 mouse liver microsomes (0.5 mg protein/mL) and CD-1 mouse cryopreserved hepatocytes (0.5 million cells/mL)) ; 7-Ethoxycoumarin: 808 min (pH 1.3), 991 min (pH 5.5), 705 min (pH 7.4) (0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer)
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS: Waters XSELECT HSS T3 2.5 µm 30 x 2.1 mm column with formic acid water/acetonitrile gradient, detected on an Applied Biosystems Sciex API-5500 triple quadrupole mass spectrometer with positive-ion electrospray ionization, multiple-reaction-monitoring; RT-PCR/SYBR Green used for CYP450 mRNA induction endpoints
notes: Pure ADME stability-characterization study; no animal or human was dosed, so there are no in vivo PK parameters (no Cmax, Tmax, AUC, dose or route). Only half-lives from incubations are available. Full set of HM-10/10 half-lives reported in the body: plasma (Table 1) human 164 min, Sprague-Dawley rat 82.5 min, beagle dog 54.6 min, cynomolgus monkey 52.7 min, CD-1 mouse 5.68 min; simulated gastric fluid 372 min and simulated intestinal fluid 2.72 min (Table 2); buffer pH 1.3 and 5.5 could not be determined (>120 min), pH 7.4 = 433 min (Table 3); liver microsomes (Table 4) CD-1 mouse 32.0 min, rat 27.7 min, dog 33.0 min, monkey 21.8 min, human 20.3 min; hepatocytes (Table 5) CD-1 mouse <15 min, rat 5.81 min, dog 10.7 min, monkey 12.1 min, human 5.28 min. Note the PEPLIFE2 header row lists 32.5 min for CD-1 mouse liver microsomes whereas Table 4 in the body states 32.0 min; the body value was used. Plasma protein binding in CD-1 mouse was 15.3 +/- 24.6% bound (Table 6). CYP450 positive-control inhibitors and inducers are listed as reference-standard agents; substrate probes (phenacetin, bupropion, amodiaquine, diclofenac, mephenytoin, dextromethorphan, midazolam, testosterone) and internal standards (carbutamide, chrysin, glyburide, Feng#1 SIL) were also used but are analytical reagents rather than tested articles. Body reports no ex vivo/in vitro half-life for warfarin or for the CYP control compounds.

half_life_summaries: CLA-coated PTX-SPIONs@HRH: 17.1 h (mouse plasma (PTX measured; heparin-flushed tubes, cardiac puncture)) ; Taxol (commercial paclitaxel formulation): 9.0 h (mouse plasma)
bioanalytical_method: High performance liquid chromatography with UV detection at 227 nm (Flexar LC UV/VIS, PerkinElmer), after liquid-liquid extraction of plasma with 1.25% v/v ethanol in diethyl ether and docetaxel as internal standard; Waters C18 column (250 x 3.9 mm, 5 μm), 20 μL injection, 1.9 mL/min
concentration_time_locator: Figure 10 (also Figure 4 for in vitro release)
notes: UNIT-HEADER CHECK: the PK table has two separate columns, 'T1/2 (h)' and 'Kel (h-1)'. The half-life values recorded here (17.1 h and 9.0 h) come from the column named T1/2 (h) and are confirmed in the Results text as half-lives ('The half-life (T1/2) of commercial PTX was estimated to be 9.0 h'). The elimination rate constants Kel = 0.03 h-1 (nanoformulation) and Kel = 0.07 h-1 (Taxol) are recorded verbatim here and were NOT converted to half-lives. The paper names no kinetic phase for T1/2, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and half_life_elimination is left 'not reported', even though the adjacent Kel column is labelled 'elimination rate constant' in the table footnote. Dosing was subcutaneous, so an absorption phase exists and the body states 'PTX from CLA-coated PTX-SPIONs@HRH is slowly absorbed and released into plasma following SC injection', but no absorption half-life was fitted or reported. The PK measurand is paclitaxel, not the HRH peptide. Plasma sampling was destructive (mice euthanized at each of t = 0.5, 1, 4, 8, 24 h) with n = 3 per group. The antitumor study used a 10-fold lower PTX dose for Taxol (1.2 mg/kg) than the nanoformulation dose (12 mg/kg), matched to the 10% drug loading capacity; the PK study states 'equivalent PTX dosage' without giving a number.

half_life_summaries: BI-3434 (lipidated long-acting secretin analog): not reported as t1/2; Results report a mean residence time (MRT) of 6 h and the Discussion states half-life increased 'by more than 100x up to 6 h in mice' (mouse plasma) ; Stapled secretin (lactam-bridged secretin analog): <15 min (mouse plasma (after i.v. injection)) ; Native human secretin: not reported for this study; the Introduction cites a literature half-life of 3 min for secretin (None)
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS (solid phase extraction on OASIS MAX or WCX uElution plate, Aeris WIDEPORE column, ABSciex 6500+ Triple Quad in positive ionization mode)
concentration_time_locator: Fig. S2A (stapled secretin) and Fig. S2B (BI-3434); supplementary figures, captions not reproduced in the body text
notes: No numeric elimination half-life (t1/2) is reported for BI-3434 in the body; the Results give MRT, Cmax and tmax and the Discussion refers loosely to a half-life 'up to 6 h'. Stapled secretin has only an upper-bound half-life (<15 min) after i.v. dosing and no other PK parameters. Peptide sequences appear only in the Figure 1 structure image, which is not transcribed in the text, so all sequences are recorded as not reported. The freshly isolated mouse adipocyte lipolysis assay is called 'in vitro' by the authors but was classified ex vivo per protocol; the cell-line cAMP assay is the unambiguous in vitro component. Several body paragraphs in the source file were truncated at 2000 characters.

half_life_summaries: peptide SLAFVDVLN (BACE-1 inhibitor derived from Merluccius productus): 0.69 h (Table 4; described in the Results text as a short half-life of 0.7 h) (mouse plasma (healthy adult male Swiss mice, retro-orbital blood, EDTA))
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS: UPLC (Waters) with a Luna C18 column (5 μm, 150 × 4.6 mm), 70% methanol/0.05% formic acid isocratic elution, coupled to an ESI-Xevo TQ-S triple quadrupole in positive ionisation mode; six-point calibration curve (0.1-20 μg/mL plasma, 5-40 μg/mL organs) with 1/x2 weighted linear regression
notes: Full Table 4 PK set, quoted verbatim: t1/2 0.69 h; Cp0 2,595.96 μg/L; V 0.00154 (mg/kg)/(μg/L); CL 0.00154 (mg/kg)/(μg/L)/h; AUC 0-t 2,595.96 μg/L*h; AUC 0-inf 2,595.96 μg/L*h; AUMC 2,595.96 μg/L*h^2; MRT 1 h; Vss 0.00150 mg/kg/(μg/L). DATA-QUALITY FLAG: Cp0, AUC 0-t, AUC 0-inf and AUMC are all printed as the identical number 2,595.96 despite carrying four different units, which is almost certainly a transcription error in the published table; the values are recorded exactly as printed and no attempt was made to correct or recompute them. The AUC field therefore should be treated as unreliable. Because this was an intravenous bolus there is no absorption phase; no Cmax or tmax parameter is reported, so both are 'not reported'. Cp0 (2,595.96 μg/L) is a back-extrapolated concentration at time zero from the compartmental fit and was deliberately NOT entered as Cmax. The nearest body statement about a peak is in the Discussion: 'The peptide was found in the plasma at all analyzed times, with the highest concentration 5 min after the injection, and decreased over time, typical of an intravenous administration' - 5 min was simply the earliest post-dose sampling point, so it is not recorded as a tmax. half_life_phase is 'unspecified': the Methods say only that parameters were 'calculated in a compartmental analysis of plasma data after the intravenous bolus input' and the paper never names an alpha, beta, distribution or elimination phase, so no phase was inferred and both phase-specific half-life fields are 'not reported'. No rate constant is printed anywhere, so no ln2/k conversion was needed. SEPARATE IN SILICO VALUE, DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: Table 1 ('Properties of the peptide estimated computationally') lists 'Half-life (h) 1.90', repeated in the Results as 'Moreover, it has a half-life of 1.9 h'. That is a ProtParam/ExPASy prediction, not a measurement, and was not used for any half-life field. The Discussion notes the measured value was 'similar to the value calculated by the computational model'. Tissue distribution from the dosed animals (spleen, liver, lung, kidney, brain; peptide absent from pancreas; brain peak at 2 h) is an in vivo biodistribution readout on harvested organ lysates and was not classified as ex vivo. Molecular docking, ProtParam and ToxinPred analyses are in silico and are not representable in the study_types vocabulary.

half_life_summaries: NCL30 (non-cross-linked, quenched pSar200-b-pCys(SO2Et)30 micelle): 11.4 h (95% CI 6.8-18.7 h) (C57BL/6 mouse blood plasma) ; 2F-CL30 (bifunctionally cross-linked CCPM, dihydrolipoic acid hydrazide): 11.3 h (95% CI 7.4-17.1 h) (C57BL/6 mouse blood plasma) ; 3F-CL30 (trifunctionally cross-linked CCPM, Cys/Sar pentapeptide): 19.1 h (95% CI 12.3-34.8 h) (C57BL/6 mouse blood plasma)
bioanalytical_method: Fluorescence quantification of the Atto647N label in plasma using a Tecan Spark plate reader (ex 640 nm / em 670 nm); ex vivo organ biodistribution by IVIS Spectrum fluorescence imaging.
notes: In vivo PK was run only for the three CL30-series particles (NCL30, 2F-CL30, 3F-CL30); the CL17 series and PM30 were characterised only in buffer and human plasma, so Table 1 leaves their t1/2 cells blank. The authors state the differences in half-life were not significant and that normalisation to the 10 min timepoint may have missed an early drop. The permitted animal-work reference is AVD1060020187085 (Leiden University). No Cmax/Tmax were computed because data were normalised to the 10 min value rather than reported as absolute concentrations.

half_life_summaries: QQT*-IRDye800: 3.6 h (stability half-life in mouse serum, not a plasma elimination half-life) (serum obtained from a CPC;Apc mouse, incubated at 37 °C (ex vivo stability assay, RP-HPLC peak area))
bioanalytical_method: Analytical RP-HPLC with peak-area quantification for serum stability; NIR fluorescence imaging for all in vivo and organ measurements, using a modified rigid small-animal endoscope (lambda-ex 785 nm) and a Pearl Trilogy imager (lambda-ex 785 nm, lambda-em 820 nm)
notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE HALF-LIFE. The only half-life in the body, 3.6 h, comes from incubating the peptide in serum harvested from a CPC;Apc mouse at 37 °C and following it by RP-HPLC over 24 h. It is a proteolytic stability half-life measured ex vivo, not a plasma elimination half-life from a dosed animal, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and both half_life_absorption and half_life_elimination are 'not reported'. The paper's own section heading 'In Vivo Serum Stability' is misleading relative to its Methods; the matrix field records the assay as it was actually performed. No plasma or blood concentrations were ever measured in this study, so there is no Cmax, tmax or AUC. The in vivo pharmacokinetics section is entirely imaging-based: 'Quantified intensities showed a peak T/B ratio at 1 h after injection of QQT*-IRDye800. The signal decreased to the baseline by ~24 h post-injection', and Figure 5a gives 'a mean (±SD) value of 2.2 ± 0.4 at 1 h post-injection with clearance by ~24 h'. That 1 h peak is a tumour-to-background fluorescence ratio maximum, not a plasma tmax, so it was deliberately not entered in the tmax field. Dose is reported only as a concentration and volume (200 μM, 200 μL); no body weight normalised dose is given. Human involvement was limited to donor-derived colonoid tissue (adenoma from a 46-year-old male and a 64-year-old male, normal colon from a 43-year-old female deceased donor) cultured in vitro; no human subject was dosed, so clinical_detail is null. Biodistribution at 1 h showed strong kidney signal consistent with renal clearance, with increased liver and lung intensity attributed to vasculature; no toxicity was seen on necropsy, hematology or chemistry at 48 h.

half_life_summaries: IL-15-Cy7 (Cy7-labeled recombinant mouse IL-15): 0.69 h (mouse blood (Cy7 fluorescence in blood samples after i.v. injection)) ; biNV-IL-15-Cy7 (Cy7-labeled biomimetic nanovaccine with membrane-bound IL-15): around 5.66 h (mouse blood (Cy7 fluorescence in blood samples after i.v. injection))
bioanalytical_method: Fluorescence spectrophotometry of the Cy7 label in blood/organ lysate (PerkinElmer), quantified against a standard curve; PK parameters computed with DAS 2.1.1 software
notes: PK (t1/2, AUC) was reported only for the Cy7-labeled agents (IL-15-Cy7 and biNV-IL-15-Cy7); no dose amount for the PK arm is given in the body. Body reports a 6.6-fold higher AUC for biNV-IL-15-Cy7 versus free IL-15-Cy7 but no absolute AUC value. No amino acid sequence, SMILES or CAS is printed anywhere in the body for IL-15 or the vesicle components. D-luciferin (3 mg per mouse, i.p.) and isoflurane/anesthetics were administered but are imaging substrate/anesthesia rather than test agents and were not listed as agents. Several body paragraphs in the source file were truncated at 2000 characters, so some mid-paragraph detail may be missing.

half_life_summaries: biotinylated scFv9-CD (anti-Abeta scFv9 fused to the 126-aa C1qTNF3 collagen domain): 1.82 h (mouse plasma (female B6C3F1)) ; biotinylated scFv9 (anti-Abeta single-chain variable fragment): 0.74 h (mouse plasma (female B6C3F1))
bioanalytical_method: Direct ELISA with Abeta40 (5 μg/well) as capture and NeutrAvidin-HRP as detection, against a purified scFv standard
notes: PK was measured only for biotinylated scFv9 and scFv9-CD after a single 250 μg IP dose; no PK was measured for scFvB11, scFvB11-CD, scFv12, scFv12-CD or CD alone. Half-life was 'calculated by nonlinear regression analysis of one-phase decay', i.e. a single-phase fit, and the paper never names the phase, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and both half_life_absorption and half_life_elimination are left 'not reported' per protocol - the 0.74 h and 1.82 h values must not be read as fitted elimination-phase parameters. No error terms, Cmax, tmax or AUC are reported. Note that the route is intraperitoneal, so an absorption phase certainly exists physiologically but was not modelled or reported. Internal inconsistency in the body: Figure 1D/1E label scFv12 as 'against N-terminal a-syn', while Figures 4-7 and the accompanying Results describe scFv12 as an anti-Abeta scFv derived from mAb 2B12; both usages are recorded as-is. Figure 6B legend writes 'scFvB12' where the Results text uses 'scFv12'. The Figure 3H caption states 100 mM Abeta42 whereas the Methods state 100 μM. The rAAV titre in the Methods is printed as '(10e genomes per milliliter)', which appears garbled in the source text, so no titre is recorded. The PEPLIFE2 header lists full scFv9 and scFv9-CD sequences, but that is database metadata and the body prints no sequences, so sequence is 'not reported' except for the ISEVKMDAEFRH immunogen fragment which is printed in the Figure 4A caption. Role 'other' is used for the immunogen and for synthetic Abeta42 because the protocol role enum does not cover immunogens or assay substrates.

half_life_summaries: Au_CR (Cys-Arg-NH2-conjugated gold nanoparticle): ~17.5 h (not reported in body; the body states only 'after intravenous (iv) injection into mice' and Fig. 5A is labelled 'Pharmacokinetic profile' without naming a matrix)
bioanalytical_method: not reported
notes: The supplied full-text file contains no METHODS section and carries a truncation marker ('One or more long lines were truncated at 2000 characters'), so dosing details, animal numbers per PK group, sample matrix and the bioanalytical assay are not recoverable from the body. The only PK datum in the body is the ~17.5 h half-life for Au_CR after intravenous injection, with no phase named, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and both half_life_absorption and half_life_elimination are left as not reported rather than inferred. No Cmax, tmax, AUC or rate constant appears anywhere in the body. The PEPLIFE2 header states the matrix as mice plasma and the assay as ICP-MS; that is database metadata and was not used, so half_life_matrix and bioanalytical_method are recorded as not reported. Group size for the PK panel is given only as 'three independent experiments', not as animals per group. ex_vivo_origin is 'not reported' because the body does not state the species of the plasma used in the 24 h stability incubation or of the erythrocytes in the hemolysis assay. Molecular dynamics simulations (all-atom and coarse-grained) and the DOPC/DOPG vesicle work are computational and cell-free respectively and were not counted as separate study types beyond in vitro.

half_life_summaries: Ex-DARP-FGF21: 27.6 ± 3.2 hours (mouse plasma (C57BL/6) after a single subcutaneous dose)
bioanalytical_method: Sandwich ELISA (immobilized mouse monoclonal anti-exendin-4 capture antibody, rabbit anti-FGF21 detection antibody with HRP-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG), quantified against a standard curve; half-life from PKSolver in Microsoft Excel
notes: Pharmacokinetics were measured only for Ex-DARP-FGF21; no half-life, Cmax, tmax or AUC is reported for Ex-DARP, and no clearance or volume of distribution is given for either. The PK construct retained its His-tag whereas the efficacy constructs were TEV-cleaved. The body contains a dose inconsistency for the DIO repeat-dosing study: Methods 3.6 states 25 nmol/kg every three days and the Figure 6 caption states 25 nmol/kg, but the Results text states 30 nmol/kg. A mutation inconsistency also exists: Methods 3.1 states FGF21 L98R and P171A, while the Discussion states L98R and P171G. No amino-acid sequence is printed in the body; only GenBank accessions and (GGGGS)3 linkers are given. Oral glucose (2 g/kg) is a challenge agent and is not listed as a test article.

half_life_summaries: GLP-ABD-XTEN144: 12.9 ± 2.7 h (mouse plasma (C57BL/6) after a single subcutaneous dose) ; GLP-ABD-XTEN288: 7.32 ± 0.9 h (mouse plasma (C57BL/6) after a single subcutaneous dose)
bioanalytical_method: Sandwich ELISA (immobilized anti-His-tag antibody for capture, rabbit monoclonal anti-GLP-1 antibody plus HRP-linked goat anti-rabbit IgG for detection), quantified against a standard curve; half-life from PK Solver in Microsoft Excel
notes: Only a fragment of each construct's primary sequence (the TEV-GLP-1 portion) is printed in the body; the ABD (46 aa) and XTEN144/XTEN288 sequences are described only by name and length, so the full sequences are not available from the body. The PK constructs retain a C-terminal His-tag that the efficacy constructs did not, and the PK dose (5 nmol/mouse s.c.) differs from the pharmacodynamic doses (3-30 nmol/kg). PK n = 3 per group. AUC(0-inf) was 20983.3 +/- 3374.3 h x ng/mL for XTEN144 and 18652.5 +/- 4269.7 h x ng/mL for XTEN288. Oral glucose (2 g/kg) is a challenge agent and is not listed as a test article.

half_life_summaries: A1L35HR2m-Chol (cholesterol-conjugated ACE2-HR2 fusion lipopeptide): approximately 81.8 h in plasma (mouse plasma (also lung, nose and trachea homogenates)) ; A1L35HR2m (unmodified ACE2-HR2 fusion peptide): 2.6 h in plasma (mouse plasma)
bioanalytical_method: Indirect functional bioassay: serial dilution of mouse plasma or tissue homogenate followed by a SARS-CoV-2 D614G pseudovirus infection inhibition assay in Caco-2 cells, with the dilution fold achieving 50% inhibition (DF-IC50) converted to an estimated peptide concentration; pharmacokinetic parameters then computed with PKSolver software. No LC-MS/MS, ELISA or radiolabel assay is described.
concentration_time_locator: Fig. 5B (plasma) and Fig. 5D (lung, nose, trachea homogenates); Fig. 5A and 5C show the underlying dilution-fold time courses
notes: Dosing for the PK study was intranasal, so an absorption phase exists, but the paper reports no absorption half-life and no absorption rate constant; half_life_absorption is therefore 'not reported' for all agents and nothing was converted. The half-lives were obtained by fitting estimated concentration-time data in PKSolver and no phase is named anywhere, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and half_life_elimination is left as not reported rather than inferred from an unnamed t1/2. A tmax of 8 h IS reported for A1L35HR2m-Chol in plasma, lung, nose and trachea ('The peptide concentration in the lung, nose, and trachea peaked at 8 h'), but no numeric Cmax is given in the body: the peak is expressed as a mean dilution fold (10,284-fold plasma, 58,770-fold lung, 18,231-fold nose, 1,959-fold trachea) with the estimated concentrations plotted only in Figures 5B and 5D. Tissue half-lives (lung 89.8 h, nose 49.0 h, trachea 10.6 h) are recorded in notes_agent alongside the headline plasma value of 81.8 h. Full amino-acid sequences appear only inside the Figure 1A image and in the PEPLIFE2 metadata header, so all sequence fields are recorded as not reported in body. The peptide concentration measurement is an indirect functional estimate rather than a direct analytical quantitation, which is a caveat on all reported concentrations and AUCs. Live SARS-CoV-2 isolates came from patient specimens, but no human was dosed, so the study is not classified as clinical. The virus challenge inocula (Omicron BA.5 and EG.5.1 at 10,000 PFU, SARS-CoV-2 Alpha at 200 PFU) are model-induction agents and are noted here rather than listed as agent objects.

half_life_summaries: ABD035-immunoGN (P1h3-ABD035-B2-E5C3-GN-His): approximately 30 min (stated as a 7-fold increase over immunoGN) (mouse serum (text says nude mice; Methods say BALB/c mice)) ; dAb7h8-immunoGN (P1h3-dAb7h8-B2-E5C3-GN-His): approximately 30 min (stated as a 7-fold increase over immunoGN) (mouse serum (text says nude mice; Methods say BALB/c mice)) ; immunoGN (P1h3-B2-E5C3-GN-His): less than 5 min (mouse serum)
bioanalytical_method: Cell-based ELISA: serum samples applied to fixed SKBR-3 cells, detected with an anti-His mouse antibody plus HRP-conjugated anti-mouse antibody and TMB substrate.
notes: Numeric half-lives are never printed in the body; only 'less than 5 min' (immunoGN) and 'approximately 30 min' / 'as short as 30 min' (ABD035-immunoGN and dAb7h8-immunoGN) with a stated 7-fold increase. The precise per-agent minute values in the PEPLIFE2 header are NOT supported by the body. There is an internal inconsistency about the PK strain and group size: Methods say 'four groups of five female BALB/c mice each', the Results say 'the serum of nude mice', the Discussion says 'confirmed in nude mice', and the Fig. 3D caption says 'n = 3 mice per group'. The file header carries 'PMID: ?' and PMC11088320; the PMID was supplied by the assignment. The DyLight 800 tracing figure (Fig. 4B) caption says imaging was 24 h after injection whereas the Methods say the labelled proteins were injected for 10 min.

half_life_summaries: (89Zr, Mn)-WPMNs (89Zr-radiolabelled, Mn2+-chelated, WL12-SH- and PEG-modified melanin nanoparticles): metabolic half-life 0.1234 h and distribution half-life 1.554 h (KM mouse blood (samples collected from the orbital vein))
bioanalytical_method: Radioactivity measurement of weighed blood samples with a gamma-counter (89Zr); pharmacokinetic parameters fitted in GraphPad Prism 9.0
notes: PK is reported for (89Zr, Mn)-WPMNs only. The body reports two half-lives with non-standard phase names: 'metabolic half-life' 0.1234 h and 'distribution half-life' 1.554 h. Note the naming is inverted relative to the usual convention - here the faster value is called metabolic and the slower value distribution - and the paper never uses the words 'elimination' or 'terminal'. Both values are therefore recorded verbatim in half_life with half_life_phase 'unspecified', and half_life_absorption and half_life_elimination are left 'not reported' rather than mapping the slow phase onto elimination. Dosing was intravenous, so no absorption phase exists. Both are stated as half-lives in hours, not rate constants. No error terms, Cmax, tmax or AUC are reported for the blood PK; the reported concentrations elsewhere are biodistribution %ID/g at fixed timepoints (liver 39.43 ± 10.03 %ID/g, spleen 25.19 ± 0.43 %ID/g at 24 h). Group size for the PK cohort is not stated. Two different 89Zr physical half-lives appear in the body for context ('89Zr (1/2t=78.4 h)' in the INTRO); the abstract's 100.8 h value was not used. The WL12-SH amino-acid sequence is not printed in the body and the PEPLIFE2 header sequence field is blank, so sequence is 'not reported'. Anaesthetics (isoflurane, 4% chloral hydrate) and the 808 nm laser irradiation are procedural interventions and are not listed as agents.
